extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Central Reexamination Unit staff, and patent prosecution/legal staff handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for conducting, suspending, preparing, and concluding inter partes reexamination proceedings (including NIRC preparation, examiner amendments, publication, and certificates). Targeted to USPTO examiners and reexamination unit personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 317(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'raised or could have raised' applies only to patent claims that were in suit and for which a final decision on non-invalidity has been entered. Once the claims that were actually before the court at the time of the court's decision are determined, the statute prohibits the Office from maintaining an inter partes reexamination of any such patent claim on the basis of issues which the requester raised or could have raised in the litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence showing which claims were before the court may include a copy of the jury verdict form, other court documents, and docket entries. The petitioner must show that the issue(s) raised in the reexamination proceeding are the same issue(s) that were raised or could have been raised by the requester in the civil action. The requester may still assert invalidity based on newly discovered prior art unavailable to the requester at the time of the civil action; the patent owner bears the burden of showing a reference was 'available' (i.e., known to the requester) at a time it could have been raised (e.g., prior to trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-cause suspension due to pending litigation (pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 314(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may suspend inter partes reexamination proceedings for 'good cause' pending the conclusion of litigation where there is potential for termination of the reexamination prosecution under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 317(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants of suspensions are extremely rare. The Office must consider the special dispatch requirement and weigh the probability of reversal on appeal and time to final resolution. Any suspension request is resolved case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider when determining 'good cause' to suspend
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether there is 'good cause' to suspend action in the reexamination based on pending litigation, the Office may consider the following elements: (1) requester is a party to the litigation; (2) claims at issue in litigation are identical to the claims under reexamination; (3) issues raised in reexamination are the same issues that were raised or could have been raised in the litigation; (4) litigation has advanced to a late enough stage with sufficient probability of a final adverse decision to the requester; (5) there is a concurrent ex parte reexamination for the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Element (2) emphasizes estoppel applies only to patent claims litigated in the suit. For element (3), new art that could not have been raised in litigation does not trigger estoppel. For element (5), concurrent ex parte reexamination may allow the Office to proceed (Ethicon v. Quigg), and consultation with OPLA is recommended. Each factor is fact-specific and should be weighed together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence to show availability/knowledge of prior art to requester
rubrics_metrics.description: To show that a reference is 'available' the patent owner must provide sufficient evidence that the reference was known to the requester (actual knowledge) at a time when it could have been raised in the civil action (e.g., prior to any trial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: copy of jury verdict form listing prior art raised at trial; defendant's invalidity contentions listing prior art known to the requester before trial; comparison between prior art raised in reexamination and prior art raised at trial. The petitioner may provide discussion/comparison of prior art raised in reexamination and any prior art actually raised at trial, accompanied by court documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rare nature of suspension grants and timing considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant of a petition to suspend an inter partes reexamination proceeding pending potential termination due to litigation is extremely rare because it is difficult to determine the likelihood and timing of appellate reversal or final resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is less likely when reexamination proceedings are far along; delay by requester in filing reexamination requests (e.g., waiting until after district court judgment) weighs against requester. Case law (e.g., Sony v. Dudas) recognizes 'good cause' in fact-specific scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner litigation review responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner is responsible for conducting a reasonable investigation for evidence as to whether the patent for which reexamination is requested has been, or is, involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation should include review of the reexamination file, the patent file, and results of litigation computer searches. If awareness of PTAB review proceedings exists, refer the reexamination to the examiner's SPRS to coordinate with PTAB before taking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with PTAB Review Proceedings (AIA 315(d)/325(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the pendency of an inter partes review, post grant review or covered business method review, if another proceeding (e.g., reexamination) or matter involving the patent is before the Office, the Director may determine how the PTAB Review Proceeding and the other proceeding may proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner becomes aware of a PTAB Review Proceeding for the same patent being reexamined, the reexamination must be referred to the examiner's SPRS who will coordinate with the PTAB before any action is taken on the reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances when a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) is appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The only instances when issuance of a NIRC action would be proper in an inter partes reexamination proceeding are: (A) no timely response by patent owner to an Office action requiring a response (all claims under rejection -> cancel all claims), (B) after a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) where no party timely files a notice of appeal, (C) after filing of a notice of appeal where appellants fail to timely file an appellant brief or complete it, (D) after a final decision by the Board where there is no further timely appeal to the Federal Circuit nor timely request for rehearing by the Board, (E) after the federal court appeal process has been completed and case is returned to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form PTOL-2068; attach examiner's amendment as needed to cancel claims; reasons for patentability required for patentable claims; follow panel review procedures when at least one claim is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of NIRC when no allowed claims exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Where all claims are rejected or objected to in the prior Office action, the examiner will issue a NIRC indicating that all claims have been canceled and terminating the prosecution. The examiner will draft an examiner's amendment canceling all live claims and check the appropriate box on PTOL-2068.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the remarks of the examiner’s amendment, point out why the claims have been canceled. No reasons for patentability are attached. No panel review conference is needed in this ministerial instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of NIRC when at least one claim is allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If at least one claim is free of rejection and objection, the examiner will issue a NIRC identifying all patentable claims and canceled claims; rejected or objected claims will be canceled by formal examiner's amendment. Reasons for patentability must be provided for all patentable claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will draft a preliminary NIRC and inform CRU SPRS or TC QAS; a panel review conference will be convened and conference members will review patentability pursuant to MPEP §2671.03. If the conference confirms the examiner's decision the NIRC is issued and signed with conferees initialing; if not, the examiner re-evaluates and issues an appropriate Office action. Panel review is not held for claims already reviewed by Board or federal court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on examiner's amendments accompanying a NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are not permitted in an inter partes reexamination; examiner's amendments accompanying the NIRC may only be made where authorization need not be obtained and are limited to formal matters or other specified situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted examiner's amendments include: (A) formal matters (grammar, spelling, incorrect number) that do not involve a rejection or merits; (B) change the title; (C) cancel all rejected and objected claims when patent owner fails to timely respond/appeal/act; (D) if patent expires during the proceeding, withdraw amendments and include a statement that amendments are improper. Changes going to the merits cannot be made by such an amendment; they require reopening prosecution, office action suggesting the change, formal amendment by patent owner, and opportunity for third-party comments. Examiner's amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-text presentation requirement for examiner's amendments in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's amendment requires presentation of the full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed, with 37 CFR 1.530(f) markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners' amendments in reexamination are not subject to exceptions provided for applications under 37 CFR 1.121(g). The only exception: an entire claim or paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting it without presenting the text. If a portion of the text is amended more than once, indicate all changes (insertions and deletions) in relation to the current text in the patent under reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for patentability must be provided for every claim identified as patentable in the NIRC, unless all claims are canceled in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate why the claims found patentable are clearly patentable over the cited patents or printed publications, similar to reasons for allowance in an application (see MPEP §1302.14). Examiner may refer to portions of the record that establish patentability. Reasons may be set forth on Form PTOL-476 or by using form paragraph 26.70. Patent owner must be notified in the NIRC that it may provide comments on the statement of reasons for patentability/confirmation; comments will be placed in the reexamination file without comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of the reexamination file for publication and checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete preparation of the case for reexamination certificate by completing Examiner Checklist Reexamination form PTOL-1516, and the Legal Instrument Examiner (LIE) must complete Reexamination Clerk Checklist form PTOL-1517; the case is reviewed by CRU SPRS/TC QAS and forwarded to Office of Data Management for printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow guidance in MPEP §2287 for preparing inter partes reexamination certificate for publication. After review, NIRC is mailed and PALM work and scanning updates are performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination reminders — substantive checklist items
rubrics_metrics.description: Before forwarding for processing of the NIRC, the examiner should ensure certain items have been correctly completed or followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items to ensure: (A) All patent claims for which a substantial new question of patentability or reasonable likelihood of prevailing had been found must have been examined (see MPEP §2643). (B) No renumbering of patent claims is permitted (new claims may require renumbering; see MPEP §§2666.01 and 2250). (C) Amendments to description and claims must conform to 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(k). (D) Prior art must be listed on approved forms (PTO-892, PTO-1449, PTO/SB/08A/08B, PTO/SB/42 or equivalent) (see MPEP §2657). (E) Examiner and clerk checklists PTOL-1516 and PTOL-1517 must be entirely and properly completed and cross-checked. (F) Multiple copending reexamination proceedings are often merged (see MPEP §2686.01). (G) If copending with a reissue application, files must be forwarded to OPLA for potential merger with decision in file (see MPEP §2686.03). (H) Reasons for patentability/confirmation are required for each claim found patentable. (I) There is no issue fee in reexamination (see MPEP §2634). (J) Patent claims may not be amended nor new claims added after expiration of the patent (see MPEP §§2666.01 and 2250). (K) Original drawings cannot be physically changed; amended or new figures must be labeled and on new sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 (see 37 CFR 1.530(d)(3) and MPEP §2666.02). (L) An amended or new claim may not enlarge the scope of the patent claims (see MPEP §§2658, 2666.01, and 2250). (M) If the patent has expired, all amendments made during the proceeding must be withdrawn and presently rejected and objected claims canceled (see MPEP §2250).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multiple dependent claims for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of multiple dependent claims when preparing a reexamination proceeding for publication is addressed and should follow the discussion in MPEP §2287.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §2287 for specifics on how multiple dependent claims are to be presented in preparation for issuing the reexamination certificate and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on changing the title of the patent during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally the title will not need to be changed during reexamination. If a change of the title is necessary, it should have been pointed out as early as possible in prosecution as part of an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal examiner's amendment (e.g., simply changing the title and initialing) is not permitted in reexamination; title changes should be handled following proper Office action procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when all claims are canceled
rubrics_metrics.description: When all claims in the reexamination proceeding are to be canceled (e.g., patent owner fails to timely respond, or Board decision affirms rejections and appeals time has expired), examiner will issue a NIRC indicating all claims canceled and terminating prosecution. Examiner will draft an examiner's amendment canceling all live claims and explain why in the remarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a scanned copy of claims with brackets and place in file history. Panel review is not held. Examiner will designate a canceled original patent claim to be printed in Official Gazette on the Issue Classification IFW form.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interviews permitted in inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are not permitted in an inter partes reexamination proceeding; the examiner is not permitted to telephone the patent owner to obtain authorization to make an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All communications must follow written procedures. The only examiner's amendments that can be made without patent owner authorization are limited formal matters (see allowed categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of submissions after NIRC — petition and approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules do not provide for an amendment to be filed in an inter partes reexamination proceeding after a NIRC has been issued except by petition under 37 CFR 1.182; 37 CFR 1.312 does not apply. Any amendment, IDS, or other paper related to merits filed after the NIRC must be accompanied by a petition which must be granted to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition under 37 CFR 1.182 is granted, examiner will reconsider in view of new information and may reopen prosecution. Examiner's amendments after NIRC are limited to minor formal matters and require CRU SPRS or TC QAS approval to withdraw an issued NIRC for issuance of a new one. 'Comments on Statement of Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation' received are placed in file without comment even if certificate already issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance and content requirements for inter partes reexamination certificate (35 U.S.C. 316; 37 CFR 1.997)
rubrics_metrics.description: At conclusion of inter partes reexamination, Director shall issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined unpatentable, confirming claims determined patentable, and incorporating in the patent any proposed amended or new claim determined patentable. The certificate concludes the proceeding and must be issued/published for each patent where a reexamination proceeding was ordered, except where proceeding vacated or replaced by reissue patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate will be sent to patent owner (per §1.33(c)) and third party requester; notice of issuance published in Official Gazette. If certificate cancels all claims, no further Office proceedings will be conducted with that patent or related reissue/reexamination requests. A reissued patent may serve as the reexamination certificate where applicable.
